fixes.explanation: Right, friend. Jesus says, “On My account you will stand before governors and kings as witnesses to them.” They're called witnesses, not judges. They stand there on His account, and that's the part that matters.

Jesus says, “And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.” Notice the word “first.” The gospel goes out to all the nations, and Jesus puts that first. Big job. Good thing it's not mine to bake alone.

Good guess, friend, but law isn't the word Jesus uses. He says, “And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.” The word is gospel, and it's going out to every nation. That's the word to hang onto here.

Psalms are lovely, and a psalm is a fine thing to hum over the dough. But Jesus doesn't name them here. He says, “And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.” Gospel is the word, and it's meant for all the nations.
Jesus says, “…then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.” He means for them to move, and He says where. The mountains are the place He names. When Jesus says go, friend, it's time to go.
That's right. Jesus says, “And let no one in the field return for his cloak.” The one in the field doesn't turn back. Whatever is back there stays there.

Jesus says the opposite. “…for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen, He has cut them short.” He doesn't stretch out that time of tribulation, He cuts it short. And He does it for the sake of the elect.

Jesus says, “…to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” The word “even” points to the elect as the ones these false Christs and false prophets are after. Those are His words, so they're worth hearing twice. That's why He tells them to be on guard.

The scribes are a fair guess, friend, but they're not in this warning. Jesus says the false Christs and false prophets will try “…to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” Earlier He calls the elect the ones “whom He has chosen” (Mark 13:20). Those are the people this warning is about.

The Romans don't come up in this warning, friend. Jesus says the false Christs and false prophets will try “…to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.” Back in verse 20 He describes the elect as the ones “whom He has chosen” (Mark 13:20). So the warning is aimed at God's chosen people.
